title: Separable Verbs
sourceNote: The captions drop most of the German verbs and example sentences in this lesson. The verb list (mitkommen, mitbringen, anrufen, ankommen, anfangen, einladen, fernsehen, aufstehen, losgehen) was rebuilt from the teacher's description of the prefixes; the example sentences follow the rules he states.
objectives: I can explain what a separable verb (trennbares Verb) is
I can put the conjugated verb in position 2 and the prefix at the end
I can use separable verbs in questions and with modal verbs
I can conjugate and use common separable verbs

expressions.en: I would like to get up at 7.

patterns.en: I would like to get up at 6.

grammar.title: What are separable verbs?
grammar.body:
The verb **trennen** means 'to separate', so **trennbare Verben** are verbs that can be separated. Such a verb has two parts: a **prefix** and a normal verb. *auf* + *stehen* = **aufstehen**; *los* + *gehen* = **losgehen**.

Adding a prefix changes the meaning: *stehen* = to stand, **aufstehen** = to get up; *gehen* = to go, **losgehen** = to set off.

In the dictionary you find the whole verb together, as one word (**aufstehen**).
grammar.ar: الفعل المنفصل = بادئة + فعل عادي، والمعنى يتغير بالبادئة.

grammar.title: Position in the sentence
grammar.body:
In a statement the **conjugated verb** is in **position 2** and the **prefix** goes to the **end** of the sentence: *Ich stehe um 6 Uhr **auf**.*

In a **yes/no question** the conjugated verb is first and the prefix is still at the end: *Stehst du um 6 Uhr **auf**?* In a **W-question** the verb is second: *Wann stehst du **auf**?*

With a **modal verb** the modal is in position 2 and the whole verb stays together in the **infinitive at the end**: *Ich möchte um 6 Uhr **aufstehen**.* The verb is then not separated.
grammar.ar: الفعل المصرَّف في المكان الثاني والبادئة في آخر الجملة؛ مع الفعل المساعد يبقى الفعل كاملًا في المصدر.

examples.en: I would like to get up at 6.

grammar.title: Conjugation of aufstehen
grammar.body: The verb part is conjugated normally (see lessons 14 and 15); the prefix does not change and stays at the end.

grammar.title: Common separable verbs
grammar.body: Irregular ones change the vowel in the verb part: *anfangen* → er fängt an, *einladen* → er lädt ein, *fernsehen* → er sieht fern.

head: Infinitive
Sentence
rows: Der Zug kommt um 8 Uhr an.
Der Film fängt um 8 Uhr an.

mistakes.why: The prefix goes to the end of the sentence.

mistakes.wrong: Ich möchte um 6 Uhr stehe auf.
mistakes.why: With a modal verb the separable verb stays together in the infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: Der Film fangt um 8 Uhr an.
mistakes.right: Der Film fängt um 8 Uhr an.

pronunciation.tip: In *fängt* and *lädt* the *ä* is like the 'e' in 'bed'.

lines.en: When do you get up tomorrow?

lines.de: Ich stehe um 7 Uhr auf. Warum?
Wir gehen um 8 Uhr los. Kommst du mit?
lines.en: We set off at 8. Are you coming along?

lines.de: Ja, gern. Ich möchte nur schnell Peter anrufen.
lines.en: Yes, gladly. I just want to quickly call Peter.

tip: Always learn the verb together with its prefix and one sentence: aufstehen – Ich stehe um 6 Uhr auf.

comprehension.q: Where does the conjugated verb stand in a statement with a separable verb?

comprehension.a: At the end of the sentence.

comprehension.q: What happens to a separable verb with a modal verb?
comprehension.a: It stays together in the infinitive at the end.

summary: A separable verb = prefix + verb: aufstehen, mitkommen, anrufen ...
Statement: conjugated verb in position 2, prefix at the end.
Yes/no question: verb first, prefix at the end.
With a modal verb: the whole verb stays in the infinitive at the end.
Irregular verbs keep their irregular forms: er fängt an, er sieht fern.
